_comment: EVERY NON-ZERO NUMBER IN THIS FILE IS AN ESTIMATE. Not one of them has been proved by a --meter run, and treating one as fact is listed under 'Common mistakes' in CLAUDE.md. A vendor's price page is a marketing document; the invoice depends on the resolution actually delivered, the seconds actually billed, and whether a retried submit charged twice. scripts/providers/pricing.mjs REFUSES to load an entry that does not carry a _comment and an explicit `estimate` flag, and refuses `estimate: false` on any non-zero price -- zero is the only price that cannot drift. When actual diverges from estimated by more than divergenceLimit, `npm run ledger` names the job. Believe the ledger, not this file.

fixture/still-v1._comment: Not an estimate, and the only kind of entry allowed to say so: the fixture provider spawns local ffmpeg and there is no counterparty to bill anyone. Zero is a fact here. It is listed rather than special-cased so the cost path -- estimate, record, compare -- is exercised end to end at $0 before a paid provider is ever wired in.

fixture/video-v1._comment: Not an estimate. Same reasoning as fixture/still-v1 -- local ffmpeg, no counterparty, zero is a fact.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/image-to-video._comment: ESTIMATE, and now a SUSPECT one. Still the 720p-derived $0.3027/s, and NOBODY HAS EVER CALLED THIS ENDPOINT. What changed on 2026-08-24 is that its sibling reference-to-video was metered and came out at $0.1386/s equivalent -- 2.18x lower -- because fal bills tokens, not seconds, and the token formula in config/credits.json turns out to be exactly right. This number is very likely wrong in the same direction and by a similar factor. It is NOT copied across from the sibling: they are different endpoints, and guessing one price from another invoice is how the wrong number got here in the first place. Meter it before trusting it. The conservative-direction argument still holds meanwhile -- overstating cost understates margin, which is the safe way round.
bytedance/seedance-2.0/image-to-video.source: derived from config/credits.json 720p estimate, itself derived from fal's published token formula, UNVERIFIED

bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-vide._comment: MEASURED 2026-08-24 against fal's usage page, and the per-second unit here is a CONVERSION that has to be understood before this number is reused. fal bills this endpoint per 1000 TOKENS at $0.014, exactly the formula config/credits.json already recorded -- tokens = w * h * seconds * 24 / 1024 -- and that formula reproduces the invoice to seven figures: two clips at 752x560 x 15.04s = 296.92k tokens = $4.156915 against fal's $4.156908. THE FORMULA WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM. This table's flattening of it was: it had no token dimension, so somebody wrote the 720p per-second rate here and it was 2.18x too high. The $0.1386 below is $2.078454 per clip divided by the 15 seconds each ordered. It is exact for a 15s clip at the raster these two RETURNED and it does not generalise -- tokens scale with pixels AND frames, so a longer or larger clip is not 0.1386 x seconds. AND THE RASTER IS THE STING: 640x480 was ORDERED (108000 tokens, $1.5120) and 752x560 was DELIVERED and BILLED (148461 tokens, $2.0785). fal charges for what it sends, not for what you asked for, so the unhonoured raster recorded in config/models.json is a 37.5% surcharge and not a cosmetic complaint.
bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-vide.meteredFrom: fal.ai/dashboard/usage-billing -- 296.92 x 1000 Tokens at $0.014 = $4.156908 across jobs 20260824-122201-af8b0d and 20260824-130457-a2e9ac
bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-vide.source: fal usage page, 2026-08-24: 296.92 x 1000 Tokens at $0.014. Per-second figure derived from the DELIVERED raster, not the ordered one.

fal/still-UNVERIFIED._comment: ESTIMATE, and a placeholder: the still model has NOT been chosen. Paul picks it at Phase 0 (docs/phase-0-validation.md), and criterion 6 measures the real number as balance-before minus balance-after. The figure below is an order-of-magnitude stand-in for an identity-preserving image model at ~1MP so the estimator has something to divide by -- it is not a quote and it is not attributed to any vendor. Replace the id and the number together, in one edit, when the model is chosen.

fal-ai/uso._comment: MEASURED 2026-08-24 against fal's own usage page: 1.00 Megapixels at $0.10 = $0.10 for the single call this endpoint ever received (job 20260823-190639-21c4cd). The old placeholder said $0.05, so it was HALF the real price -- the wrong direction to be wrong in, and a reminder that an order-of-magnitude stand-in is not a conservative one. Note fal bills this per MEGAPIXEL, not per image; at the 640x480 this repo orders, one call is ~0.31MP and was billed as 1.00, which suggests a floor. The candidate FAILED on identity anyway (CLAUDE.md section 8) so nothing here is load-bearing.
fal-ai/uso.source: fal usage page, 2026-08-24. Billed per megapixel with an apparent 1MP floor.

fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4.5/edit._comment: MEASURED 2026-08-24 and the marketing page was RIGHT, which is worth recording precisely because this file's header assumes it would not be: fal's usage page shows 2.00 Images at $0.04 = $0.08 across the two calls (jobs 20260824-093906-d39675 and 20260824-114051-4209a6), exactly the ~$0.04/edit the model page quoted on 2026-08-20. One of three prices in this file that a real invoice has now confirmed rather than corrected.
fal-ai/bytedance/seedream/v4.5/edit.source: fal usage page, 2026-08-24. Confirms the model page figure read 2026-08-20.
